chapters.title: Why visualise, and how our eyes read charts
Drill down, roll up and drill across

questions.text: Two regional managers report the same average bill (₹740) and the same standard deviation for their customers. What should you do before concluding that the customers behave alike?
options: Plot the distribution of bill values for both regions
Compare the median bills and stop there
Conclude they are alike, since mean and SD both match
Check which region has more stores
correct: Plot the distribution of bill values for both regions
questions.explanation: Matching summary numbers can hide very different shapes, just like Anscombe's quartet. A histogram or box plot of both regions will show whether the spread, skew and outliers really match.

questions.text: In Dataset IV, what produces the correlation of 0.82?
options: A single extreme point
A gentle curve in the data
Most points lying close to a straight line
Very small variance in y
correct: A single extreme point
questions.explanation: Ten points share x = 8, so on their own they have no linear trend. The one point at x = 19 creates the whole correlation.

questions.text: Why was Snow's map more convincing than the table of deaths by street?
options: It showed where deaths clustered in relation to the water pumps
It contained more data than the table
Maps are always better than tables
The table had missing deaths
correct: It showed where deaths clustered in relation to the water pumps
questions.explanation: The table and the map held the same information. The map added position, the most powerful encoding we have, so the cluster around one pump became impossible to miss.

questions.text: You want managers to compare the sales of eight stores as precisely as possible. Which encoding should you choose?
options: Position and length: bars on a common baseline
Angle: a pie chart with eight slices
Area: one circle per store
Colour intensity: a shaded table
correct: Position and length: bars on a common baseline
questions.explanation: Position on a common scale is the most accurate encoding in the Cleveland and McGill ranking. Bars sharing one baseline let the eye compare lengths directly.

questions.text: Aman Mart wants to explain how last year's ₹12 Cr revenue became this year's ₹14.5 Cr, showing each category's gain or loss along the way. Which chart fits best?
options: Waterfall chart
Pie chart
Histogram
Scatter plot
correct: Waterfall chart
questions.explanation: A waterfall starts at one total, walks through each positive and negative contribution, and lands on the new total. It is built for "bridge" questions like this.

questions.text: FoodJoe wants to see which hours on which weekdays are the busiest for orders. Which chart fits best?
options: Heatmap of weekday by hour
Stacked bar of orders by city
Pie chart of orders by weekday
KPI card of total orders
correct: Heatmap of weekday by hour
questions.explanation: Two categories (weekday and hour) and one measure (orders) is the classic heatmap setup. Busy slots show up as dark cells at a glance.

questions.text: Aman Mart wants to show how the monthly sales of its 40 stores moved over two years. Which is the best choice?
options: A heatmap (stores by month) or small multiples
A line chart with 40 coloured lines
A pie chart for each month
A 3D column chart
correct: A heatmap (stores by month) or small multiples
questions.explanation: Forty series make a line chart unreadable. A heatmap packs all 40 stores into rows, and small multiples give each store its own panel on a shared scale.

questions.text: Which of these is a distribution question?
options: How are FoodJoe delivery times spread, and how many orders take more than 40 minutes?
Which city had the most orders last month?
How did orders change month by month?
What share of orders came from Pune?
correct: How are FoodJoe delivery times spread, and how many orders take more than 40 minutes?
questions.explanation: A distribution question asks how values are spread out. The other questions are comparison, trend and part-to-whole questions.

questions.text: Which change increases a chart's data-ink ratio?
options: Removing heavy gridlines and background shading
Adding a 3D effect to the bars
Adding a legend when labels could sit on the bars
Using a different colour for every bar
correct: Removing heavy gridlines and background shading
questions.explanation: Removing ink that carries no data raises the share of ink that does. The other options add non-data ink.

questions.text: When should you use a diverging colour palette?
options: When values move above and below a meaningful midpoint, like growth versus last year
For categories with no natural order, such as regions
For a single measure that runs from low to high
Whenever there are more than six categories
correct: When values move above and below a meaningful midpoint, like growth versus last year
questions.explanation: Diverging palettes use two hues around a midpoint (zero growth, 100% of target), so the reader instantly sees which side of the line each value falls on.

questions.text: A chart compares ₹98 L and ₹102 L, with the y-axis starting at ₹96 L. Roughly what is its Lie Factor?
options: About 49
About 1
About 5
About 200
correct: About 49
questions.explanation: The data difference is 4 ÷ 98, about 4%. On the chart, the bars are 6 and 2 units tall, so the bigger bar looks 200% larger. 200% ÷ 4% ≈ 49.

questions.text: What is the most honest way to compare two measures with different units, such as ad spend and sales?
options: Index both to 100 at the start, or use two charts that share the time axis
One chart with two y-axes scaled so that the lines overlap
A pie chart for each measure
A 3D chart with one axis per measure
correct: Index both to 100 at the start, or use two charts that share the time axis
questions.explanation: Indexing puts both on the same scale of relative change. Two aligned charts also work. Dual axes let the designer invent any relationship they like.

questions.text: A store manager checks stock-outs, billing queues and cash every hour. Which type of dashboard does she need?
options: Operational
Strategic
Analytical
An annual report
correct: Operational
questions.explanation: Operational dashboards support frequent, fast decisions on day-to-day activity. They favour live numbers, alerts and exceptions.

questions.text: Where should the most important KPIs usually sit on a dashboard?
options: Top-left, where the eye lands first
Bottom-right, so they are read last
In the centre, inside a pie chart
On a separate tab
correct: Top-left, where the eye lands first
questions.explanation: Readers scan from the top-left in a Z or F pattern. Key numbers placed there get seen in the first second.

questions.text: You are looking at FY 2025-26 sales by quarter, and you click Q3 to see October, November and December. What is this?
options: Drill down
Roll up
Drill across
Dice
correct: Drill down
questions.explanation: You moved from a summary level (quarter) to a more detailed level (month) of the same Time hierarchy.

questions.text: Aman Mart's analyst moves from "Sales of Beverages in Pune, Nov 2025" to "Returns of Beverages in Pune, Nov 2025", which lives in a separate returns dataset. What is this?
options: Drill across
Drill down
Roll up
Slice
correct: Drill across
questions.explanation: The coordinates stay the same while the dataset changes. That jump between fact tables is a drill across, made possible by shared dimensions.

questions.text: Why does the Gapminder chart use a log scale for income?
options: Income grows by multiplying, so equal steps on a log axis mean equal relative gains and poorer countries are not squeezed together
A log scale makes rich countries look richer
Log scales are required for bubble charts
It hides the gap between countries
correct: Income grows by multiplying, so equal steps on a log axis mean equal relative gains and poorer countries are not squeezed together
questions.explanation: On a log axis, $1,000 to $2,000 and $20,000 to $40,000 are the same distance, both a doubling. That matches how income actually changes, and it spreads out the many countries at lower incomes.

questions.text: What is the "gap instinct"?
options: Seeing the world as two separate groups with a gap between them, when most people are actually in the middle
Leaving white space between dashboard widgets
Ignoring missing data in a time series
Starting an axis above zero
correct: Seeing the world as two separate groups with a gap between them, when most people are actually in the middle
questions.explanation: Rosling showed that most countries and most people sit in the middle of the income range. Charts that compare only two group averages can reinforce the false picture of a divided world.

questions.text: In Few's sales dashboard, why are bullet graphs used instead of speedometer gauges?
options: They show actual, target and performance bands in a small space and are easy to compare
They look more modern than gauges
They show more colour
Gauges cannot show targets
correct: They show actual, target and performance bands in a small space and are easy to compare
questions.explanation: A gauge uses a large circle to show one number. A bullet graph shows the same number plus target and bands in a thin strip, and several bullets stack neatly for comparison.

questions.text: covid19india.org used the same colour for "Confirmed" in every widget. Why does that help?
options: Readers learn the colour once and connect related widgets instantly
It makes the page look brighter
It reduces the size of the page
It is required for maps
correct: Readers learn the colour once and connect related widgets instantly
questions.explanation: Consistent colour is the Gestalt principle of similarity at work. The colour becomes a label, so readers link the counter, the map and the chart without reading.

questions.text: Four datasets share the same mean, variance, correlation and regression line. What can you conclude about them?
options: Nothing about their shape until you plot them
They are the same dataset
They all have a linear relationship
They have no outliers
correct: Nothing about their shape until you plot them
questions.explanation: This is Anscombe's lesson: identical summary statistics can hide completely different patterns.

questions.text: What was John Snow's key insight from mapping cholera deaths in 1854?
options: Deaths clustered around one water pump, pointing to contaminated water
Cholera spread through bad air from sewers
Richer streets had fewer deaths
Deaths were evenly spread across Soho
correct: Deaths clustered around one water pump, pointing to contaminated water
questions.explanation: The map showed deaths clustered around the Broad Street pump, supporting Snow's theory that cholera spread through water.

questions.text: Which visual encoding do people judge most accurately?
options: Position along a common scale
Area of circles
Angle of pie slices
Colour intensity
correct: Position along a common scale
questions.explanation: Cleveland and McGill found position on a common scale to be the most accurate, which is why bar and dot charts are so effective.

questions.text: Aman Mart wants to show how last year's revenue became this year's revenue through each category's gain or loss. Which chart fits best?
options: Waterfall chart
Scatter plot
Histogram
Heatmap
correct: Waterfall chart
questions.explanation: A waterfall walks from a starting total through each positive and negative contribution to the ending total.

questions.text: A manager wants to compare the shares of 11 product sub-categories. What is the better choice?
options: A sorted bar chart
A pie chart with 11 slices
A 3D pie chart
A line chart
correct: A sorted bar chart
questions.explanation: With many parts, pie slices become hard to rank and colours hard to match. A sorted bar chart stays readable.

questions.text: Which title is most useful on a chart shown to the regional head?
options: Dairy margin fell to 6% in Aug 2025, the lowest in two years
Dairy margin chart
Monthly margin analysis, FY 2025-26
Gross margin % by month (Dairy)
correct: Dairy margin fell to 6% in Aug 2025, the lowest in two years
questions.explanation: An action title states the insight. The reader knows what to look for and why it matters.

questions.text: You must show growth versus last year for 14 stores, some up and some down. Which colour palette fits best?
options: Diverging, centred on zero growth
Sequential, light to dark
Rainbow
A different categorical colour per store
correct: Diverging, centred on zero growth
questions.explanation: Growth has a meaningful midpoint (zero). A diverging palette shows at once which side each store falls on.

questions.text: What is wrong with this chart?
options: The y-axis starts at ₹48 L, exaggerating a small difference
The bars should be the same colour
There are too few bars
The labels should be inside the bars
correct: The y-axis starts at ₹48 L, exaggerating a small difference
questions.explanation: The real difference is about 4%, but because the axis starts at ₹48 L, one bar looks several times taller. Bar charts should start at zero.

questions.text: A news channel says sales "crashed 20%" by comparing the Diwali month with January. What is the pitfall?
options: A cherry-picked time window that ignores seasonality
A truncated y-axis
A dual axis
Too many KPIs
correct: A cherry-picked time window that ignores seasonality
questions.explanation: Comparing a festive peak with an ordinary month creates a false decline. Compare with the same month last year, or show the full history.

questions.text: Why place four KPI cards along the top-left of a dashboard?
options: The eye lands there first, so the most important numbers are seen in the first second
It leaves the centre free for decoration
KPI cards must always be the smallest widgets
It hides them from casual readers
correct: The eye lands there first, so the most important numbers are seen in the first second
questions.explanation: Readers scan in a Z or F pattern starting at the top-left. That prime space belongs to the numbers that matter most.

questions.text: Aman Mart's dashboard shows yearly sales. The analyst clicks 2025 to see quarterly figures. What is this?
options: Drill down
Roll up
Drill across
Dice
correct: Drill down
questions.explanation: Moving from year to quarter goes one level deeper in the Time hierarchy.

questions.text: From quarterly sales by city, the analyst goes back to yearly sales by region. What is this?
options: Roll up
Drill down
Drill across
Slice
correct: Roll up
questions.explanation: Rolling up re-aggregates detail into summary levels of the hierarchies.

questions.text: The analyst jumps from "Sales of Snacks in Latur, Dec 2025" to "Stock of Snacks for Latur at Madavi Warehouse, Dec 2025". Why is this possible?
options: Both datasets share the same product, location and time dimensions
Both datasets are stored in Excel
The warehouse data is a subset of sales data
Madavi Warehouse is in Latur
correct: Both datasets share the same product, location and time dimensions
questions.explanation: Drill across works when two fact tables share conformed dimensions, so the same coordinates mean the same thing in both.

questions.text: In Rosling's Gapminder bubble chart, what does the size of each bubble show?
options: Population
Income per person
Life expectancy
Region
correct: Population
questions.explanation: Bubble area shows population. Position shows income and life expectancy; colour shows region.

questions.text: What makes the Our World in Data grapher especially good for exploration?
options: Readers can switch between chart, map and table views and choose countries and years themselves
It uses 3D charts
It shows every indicator on one page
It hides sources to keep the page clean
correct: Readers can switch between chart, map and table views and choose countries and years themselves
questions.explanation: Linked views plus reader control let people ask their own questions, while visible sources keep the work checkable.

questions.text: Aman Mart wants an AI model that predicts which customers will stop coming. Its bills are spread across three billing software and many bills have no phone number. What should Aman Mart do first?
options: Bring the bills from all systems into one place and fix how customers are identified
Hire a deep learning expert to build the model straight away
Run A/B tests on discount coupons
Buy a powerful GPU server for training
correct: Bring the bills from all systems into one place and fix how customers are identified
questions.explanation: In the hierarchy of needs, collection and reliable movement and storage of data come first. A model built on scattered, incomplete data cannot be trusted.

questions.text: Which of these pieces of work is downstream of data engineering?
options: A data scientist building a demand forecast from the cleaned sales table
Designing how bills move from the counters to the warehouse
Removing duplicate bills created when a counter goes offline and resyncs
Deciding how often to pull truck locations from Niharika Logistics
correct: A data scientist building a demand forecast from the cleaned sales table
questions.explanation: The forecast uses data that data engineering has already prepared, so it sits downstream. The other three are data engineering work.

questions.text: Why does Storage run under Ingestion, Transformation and Serving in the lifecycle diagram?
options: Data is stored at every step: raw after ingestion, clean after transformation and ready-to-use for serving
Data is stored only once, at the end of the pipeline
Storage is not needed when data is streamed
Storage is handled only by the source systems
correct: Data is stored at every step: raw after ingestion, clean after transformation and ready-to-use for serving
questions.explanation: Every stage reads from and writes to storage. That is why it is drawn as a base under the other three.

questions.text: At FoodJoe, which lifecycle stage is the data engineer usually not in control of?
options: Generation: the order app and its database are run by the app development team
Ingestion: pulling orders from the app database into the lake
Transformation: joining orders with restaurant details
Serving: publishing daily order tables for analysts
correct: Generation: the order app and its database are run by the app development team
questions.explanation: Source systems belong to application teams or outside partners. The data engineer must understand them and work with their owners, but does not run them.

questions.text: Dhanvanshi copies only rows whose updated_at is later than the last run. An order was cancelled and its row deleted from the app database. What happens in the warehouse?
options: The deleted order stays in the warehouse, so sales are shown higher than they are
The pipeline removes the order automatically
The pipeline stops with an error
The order's amount becomes zero
correct: The deleted order stays in the warehouse, so sales are shown higher than they are
questions.explanation: A deleted row has no timestamp left to find. Timestamp-based loads cannot see deletes. Change data capture reads the database's change log, which records deletes too.

questions.text: Why should heavy reports not run directly on the billing counters' database?
options: It is an OLTP system built for fast small writes, and long analytical queries can slow down billing
OLTP databases cannot store decimal amounts
The billing database deletes all data every night
SQL does not allow analytical queries on OLTP systems
correct: It is an OLTP system built for fast small writes, and long analytical queries can slow down billing
questions.explanation: OLTP systems are tuned for many small transactions. Large scans compete for the same resources, so analysis is done on a copy in an OLAP system.

questions.text: For the question “total sales of Toor Dal 1 kg in 2025”, why is a column format such as Parquet faster than a row format?
options: It reads only the product and amount columns instead of every column of every row
It stores fewer rows than a row format
It keeps all the data in memory all the time
It does not need any schema
correct: It reads only the product and amount columns instead of every column of every row
questions.explanation: Column storage keeps each column together, so a query reads only the columns it needs. Columns of similar values also compress well.

questions.text: In a star schema for Dhanvanshi's sales, which of these is the fact table?
options: One row per item on each bill, with quantity and amount
One row per product, with name, brand and category
One row per branch, with city and manager
One row per date, with week, month and festival flag
correct: One row per item on each bill, with quantity and amount
questions.explanation: The fact table holds the measurements of each event. The other three are dimension tables that describe those events.

questions.text: It is November. Finance finds that GST was calculated wrongly for March and wants March sales recomputed. The counters keep bills for only 90 days. Which setup makes this easy?
options: ELT, because raw bills were loaded and kept in the warehouse
ETL, because only corrected totals were loaded
Either one, because the counters still have the March bills
Neither, because transformed data can never be recomputed
correct: ELT, because raw bills were loaded and kept in the warehouse
questions.explanation: The counters no longer have March bills. Only a setup that kept the raw data can rerun the transformation with the correct GST rule.

questions.text: Which statement about ETL and data engineering is correct?
options: ETL is one pattern within data engineering, which also covers streaming, storage design, serving, Reverse ETL and the undercurrents
Data engineering is simply a new name for ETL
ETL is used only for streaming data
Data engineering does not include moving data between systems
correct: ETL is one pattern within data engineering, which also covers streaming, storage design, serving, Reverse ETL and the undercurrents
questions.explanation: ETL covers parts of ingestion and transformation in batch. Data engineering covers the full lifecycle and the practices underneath it.

questions.text: Which Dhanvanshi use case most needs streaming data?
options: Stopping the app from accepting orders for an item that has just sold out at the store
Filing the monthly GST return
Comparing this year's branch sales with last year's
Reviewing Kavya Distributors' delivery performance every quarter
correct: Stopping the app from accepting orders for an item that has just sold out at the store
questions.explanation: Only the stock case loses value within minutes. The others work perfectly well with batch data.

questions.text: A FoodJoe order placed at 12:58 reaches the server at 13:03. Counting by event time in 5-minute tumbling windows, which window does it belong to?
questions.explanation: Event time uses when the order was actually placed. A watermark decides how long the 12:55 window waits for such late arrivals.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of Reverse ETL?
options: Sending the list of “at risk” customers from the warehouse into the WhatsApp campaign tool every morning
Copying bills from branch counters into the warehouse every night
Building a branch sales dashboard on the warehouse
Training a forecasting model on the sales table
correct: Sending the list of “at risk” customers from the warehouse into the WhatsApp campaign tool every morning
questions.explanation: Reverse ETL moves data from the warehouse back into operational tools. The first wrong option is normal ETL, and the other two are serving for analytics and ML.

questions.text: Farhan was in last week's “at risk” audience, but he visited the store 3 days ago. This week's sync runs in upsert mode. What happens to Farhan?
options: He stays in the at-risk audience and may still get a “we miss you” message
He is removed from the audience
The sync stops because his segment changed
He is moved to the Loyal audience automatically
correct: He stays in the at-risk audience and may still get a “we miss you” message
questions.explanation: Upsert only adds and updates the records it sends. Farhan is not in this week's list, so nothing touches his old record. Mirror mode would remove him.

questions.text: The Kavya invoices extract fails one night. The pipeline runs as a DAG. What happens?
options: Only tasks that depend on it, directly or indirectly, are held back; the sales dashboard still refreshes
Every task in the pipeline stops
The dependent tasks run on empty data
Only the very last task is affected
correct: Only tasks that depend on it, directly or indirectly, are held back; the sales dashboard still refreshes
questions.explanation: The orchestrator follows the arrows. Clean purchases, stock position, the demand forecast and reorder suggestions wait. Tasks with no path from the failed task run as usual.

questions.text: Which of these practices belongs to the DataOps undercurrent?
options: An automatic check that alerts the team when today's bill count is 40% below normal
Showing masked phone numbers to analysts
Choosing between a data lake and a data warehouse
Keeping all SQL code in Git with code review
correct: An automatic check that alerts the team when today's bill count is 40% below normal
questions.explanation: DataOps is about testing, monitoring and responding to problems. The others are security, data architecture and software engineering.

questions.text: Which five stages make up the data engineering lifecycle described by Reis and Housley?
options: Generation, storage, ingestion, transformation, serving
Collect, clean, model, deploy, monitor
Extract, transform, load, report, archive
Plan, build, test, release, maintain
correct: Generation, storage, ingestion, transformation, serving
questions.explanation: Generation happens in the source systems; ingestion, transformation and serving follow, with storage under all of them.

questions.text: In the data science hierarchy of needs, which layer includes cleaning and anomaly detection?
options: Explore / Transform
Move / Store
Aggregate / Label
Learn / Optimize
correct: Explore / Transform
questions.explanation: Explore and transform sits just above move and store. Cleaning and preparation happen here, before aggregation and modelling.

questions.text: Kavya Distributors renames the column “Qty” to “Quantity” in its invoice file, and the load fails. What is this called?
options: Schema drift
Data skew
A late-arriving event
A watermark
correct: Schema drift
questions.explanation: Schema drift is an unannounced change in the structure of source data. Data contracts and schema checks help catch it.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of change data capture over a nightly full load?
options: It moves only the inserts, updates and deletes, including deletes that timestamp methods miss
It does not need any access to the source database
It removes the need for a data warehouse
It cleans the data automatically
correct: It moves only the inserts, updates and deletes, including deletes that timestamp methods miss
questions.explanation: CDC reads the database's change log, so it is light and it also captures deletes.

questions.text: “Schema on read” is most closely linked with which of these?
options: A data lake
A traditional data warehouse
The billing counters' OLTP database
A star schema
correct: A data lake
questions.explanation: A lake stores files as they are and applies structure when they are read. Warehouses and OLTP databases check the schema when data is written.

questions.text: Why did ELT become popular?
options: Cloud warehouses made storage cheap and computing power easy to scale, so raw data could be loaded first and transformed inside
ETL tools stopped supporting SQL
Rules made it illegal to transform data before loading it
ELT needs no transformation at all
correct: Cloud warehouses made storage cheap and computing power easy to scale, so raw data could be loaded first and transformed inside
questions.explanation: Once storage and compute in the warehouse became cheap and elastic, keeping raw data and transforming it inside became the practical choice.

questions.text: When is transforming data before loading it still the better choice?
options: When phone numbers must be masked before any data leaves Dhanvanshi's own servers
When analysts want raw data kept for future questions
When the warehouse has plenty of cheap computing power
When business questions change very often
correct: When phone numbers must be masked before any data leaves Dhanvanshi's own servers
questions.explanation: If sensitive data must never reach the cloud unmasked, it has to be changed before the load. The other three situations favour ELT.

questions.text: UPI handled 24.51 billion transactions in August 2026. Roughly how many is that per second, on average?
options: About 9,000
About 900
About 90,000
About 9 lakh
correct: About 9,000
questions.explanation: 24.51 billion ÷ (31 days × 86,400 seconds) ≈ 9,150 transactions a second, all day and night.

questions.text: What does a 10-minute tumbling window mean?
options: Fixed 10-minute blocks that do not overlap, such as 12:00 to 12:10 and 12:10 to 12:20
A 10-minute window that moves forward every minute, so windows overlap
A window that closes after 10 minutes with no activity
The last 10 events, whatever their time
correct: Fixed 10-minute blocks that do not overlap, such as 12:00 to 12:10 and 12:10 to 12:20
questions.explanation: Tumbling windows are fixed and non-overlapping. The overlapping one is a sliding window, and the gap-based one is a session window.

questions.text: Which of these is a typical destination for Reverse ETL?
options: A CRM or marketing tool used by frontline teams
The raw layer of the data lake
A backup copy of the billing database
An archive of Parquet files
correct: A CRM or marketing tool used by frontline teams
questions.explanation: Reverse ETL delivers warehouse data into operational tools where people act on it.

questions.text: Which risk is specific to Reverse ETL?
options: Overwriting fields that staff have typed by hand into the operational tool
Losing raw data before it reaches the warehouse
Missing deleted rows in a timestamp-based load
Slow queries on columnar files
correct: Overwriting fields that staff have typed by hand into the operational tool
questions.explanation: Reverse ETL writes into live business tools. If a sync overwrites a field that sales staff maintain by hand, their work is lost.

questions.text: What does an orchestration tool such as Apache Airflow mainly do?
options: Runs tasks in the right order, retries failures and shows which step failed
Stores data in a columnar format
Replaces the need to write SQL
Encrypts data at rest
correct: Runs tasks in the right order, retries failures and shows which step failed
questions.explanation: Orchestration coordinates a DAG of tasks: dependencies, schedules, retries and visibility into each run.

questions.text: Store data: what is the support of {Bread, Butter}?
questions.explanation: Five of the ten bills (01, 02, 04, 07, 08) contain both items, so Support = 5/10 = 0.50.

questions.text: Store data: what is Confidence(Butter → Bread)?
questions.explanation: All five bills with butter also contain bread: 5/5 = 1.00. In the reverse direction, Confidence(Bread → Butter) is only 5/7 = 0.71.

questions.text: Store data: what is the lift of Tea → Bread?
questions.explanation: Confidence = 1/3 = 0.33 and Support(Bread) = 0.70, so Lift = 0.33 / 0.70 = 0.48. Tea buyers are less likely than average to buy bread.

questions.text: A rule has confidence 0.80, and its consequent appears in 80% of all bills. What is the lift, and what does it mean?
options: 1.6: strong positive association
1.0: the items are independent
0.8: negative association
It cannot be found without the support
correct: 1.0: the items are independent
questions.explanation: Lift = 0.80 / 0.80 = 1. The high confidence only shows that the consequent is a popular item.

questions.text: Which measure gives the same value for X → Y and Y → X?
options: Confidence
Lift
Both confidence and lift
Neither
correct: Lift
questions.explanation: Lift = Support(X ∪ Y) / (Support(X) × Support(Y)), which does not depend on the direction. Confidence changes because its denominator changes.

questions.text: The Apriori property states that:
options: If an itemset is frequent, all its supersets are frequent
If an itemset is infrequent, all its supersets are infrequent
Confidence always increases as itemsets grow
Lift is always above 1 for frequent itemsets
correct: If an itemset is infrequent, all its supersets are infrequent
questions.explanation: Support can only decrease as items are added, so every superset of an infrequent itemset is also infrequent. This is what makes pruning possible.

questions.text: Store data with minimum support = 3 bills: why is {Bread, Eggs, Milk} pruned without being counted?
options: Eggs appears in fewer than 3 bills
{Bread, Eggs} appears in only 2 bills
{Eggs, Milk} is not frequent
Its confidence is below 70%
correct: {Bread, Eggs} appears in only 2 bills
questions.explanation: {Bread, Eggs} has a count of 2, which is below the minimum, so no superset of it can be frequent. Eggs alone (count 4) and {Eggs, Milk} (count 3) are both frequent.

questions.text: How many association rules are possible with 6 items?
For rules made from the same frequent itemset {A, B, C}, which statement is always true?
options: Confidence(A → B, C) ≥ Confidence(A, B → C)
Confidence(A, B → C) ≥ Confidence(A → B, C)
Both confidences are always equal
Their supports are different
correct: Confidence(A, B → C) ≥ Confidence(A → B, C)
questions.explanation: Both rules have the same numerator, Support(A, B, C). The denominator Support(A, B) is at most Support(A), so Confidence(A, B → C) is at least Confidence(A → B, C).

questions.text: A rule has support 0.002 and lift 12. What should the analyst do?
options: Act on it immediately because the lift is very high
Treat it with caution because very few bills support it
Increase minimum confidence to 100%
Reject every rule whose lift is above 10
correct: Treat it with caution because very few bills support it
questions.explanation: A very high lift on a very small support usually comes from a handful of bills. The rule should be checked on more data before any action is taken.

questions.text: In which direction does money flow in the toor dal supply chain?
options: From the customer towards Latur Dal Mill (upstream)
From Latur Dal Mill towards the customer (downstream)
Only between Dhanvanshi Super Store and its customers
It does not move along the chain; each node pays only the transporter
correct: From the customer towards Latur Dal Mill (upstream)
questions.explanation: Each buyer pays its supplier: the customer pays Dhanvanshi, Dhanvanshi pays Kavya Distributors, and Kavya pays the mill. So money moves upstream, opposite to the material.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a node in the toor dal supply chain?
options: The Niharika Logistics truck route from Kavya Distributors to Madavi Warehouse
Madavi Warehouse
Arjun C&F Agent
Nithansh Stockists
correct: The Niharika Logistics truck route from Kavya Distributors to Madavi Warehouse
questions.explanation: A node is a place where stock is made, stored or sold. The truck route is a link between two nodes. Stock on the truck is pipeline stock.

questions.text: Niharika Logistics charges ₹18,000 per full truck (FTL) and ₹3 per kg for part load (PTL). Kavya Distributors has to send 4,500 kg. Which option is cheaper?
options: PTL, costing ₹13,500
FTL, costing ₹18,000
Both cost the same
FTL, because a full truck is always cheaper per kg
correct: PTL, costing ₹13,500
questions.explanation: PTL costs 4,500 × 3 = ₹13,500. The load is below the break-even of 18,000 ÷ 3 = 6,000 kg, so PTL is cheaper, though it may take a day or two longer.

questions.text: Madavi Warehouse does not have enough toor dal to meet every branch's need until the next truck. What does fair share allocation try to do?
options: Give every branch the same days of cover, so all branches run short at about the same time
Give every branch the same number of packs
Send all the stock to the branch with the highest sales
Supply the branches in the order in which their indents arrived
correct: Give every branch the same days of cover, so all branches run short at about the same time
questions.explanation: Fair share brings all branches to equal days of cover. An equal number of packs ignores the difference in demand and stock between branches.

questions.text: Five tonnes of toor dal is on a Niharika Logistics truck between Kavya Distributors and Madavi Warehouse. What type of inventory is it?
options: Pipeline (in-transit) stock
Safety stock
Anticipation stock
Dead stock
correct: Pipeline (in-transit) stock
questions.explanation: Stock that has been dispatched but not yet received is pipeline stock. It is still inventory and still blocks money.

questions.text: Madavi Warehouse doubles its order quantity for toor dal from 1,000 to 2,000 packs. Safety stock does not change. What happens?
options: Average cycle stock doubles and the number of orders per year halves
Average cycle stock halves and the number of orders per year doubles
Both average stock and the number of orders per year double
Only the safety stock goes up
correct: Average cycle stock doubles and the number of orders per year halves
questions.explanation: Average cycle stock is Q ÷ 2, so it goes from 500 to 1,000 packs. Orders per year are D ÷ Q, so they fall from 43.8 to 21.9.

questions.text: Which is the correct way to measure lead time for Madavi Warehouse?
options: From raising the order to the stock being received, checked and ready to issue
From dispatch at Kavya Distributors to arrival at Madavi Warehouse
From raising the order to dispatch at Kavya Distributors
Only the travel time of the Niharika Logistics truck
correct: From raising the order to the stock being received, checked and ready to issue
questions.explanation: Lead time covers everything between raising the order and being able to use the stock: processing, dispatch, transit, unloading, quality check and GRN.

questions.text: Madavi Warehouse needs 400 packs of an item, but the supplier's MoQ is 1,000 packs, so it orders 1,000. What happens to the extra 600 packs?
options: They stay in stock and block working capital until they are sold
They become safety stock, so the reorder point can be set to zero
The supplier takes them back at the end of the month
They reduce the lead time of the next order
correct: They stay in stock and block working capital until they are sold
questions.explanation: The extra quantity is additional cycle stock. It does not change demand or lead time, so the reorder point stays the same; the next order is simply delayed until the stock is used.

questions.text: What does a 95% cycle service level mean?
options: In 95 out of 100 order cycles, stock does not run out before the next delivery
95% of every customer's demand is met from stock
The shelf is full 95% of the time
95% of the supplier's deliveries arrive on time
correct: In 95 out of 100 order cycles, stock does not run out before the next delivery
questions.explanation: Cycle service level counts order cycles without a stock-out. The share of demand met from stock is the fill rate, a different measure.

questions.text: The lead time of an item increases from 4 days to 16 days, and daily demand variation stays the same. What happens to the safety stock?
options: It doubles
It becomes four times as large
It stays the same
It increases by 12 days of demand
correct: It doubles
questions.explanation: Safety stock depends on √L. √16 ÷ √4 = 4 ÷ 2 = 2, so safety stock doubles.

questions.text: Daily demand is 50 units, lead time is 6 days and safety stock is 40 units. What is the reorder point?
options: 340 units
300 units
260 units
90 units
correct: 340 units
questions.explanation: ROP = d × L + SS = 50 × 6 + 40 = 340 units.

questions.text: Dhanvanshi's Civil Lines branch counts its stock every Monday and orders enough to bring it up to a fixed level. Which policy is this?
options: Periodic review, order-up-to (R, S)
Continuous review, fixed quantity (s, Q)
Economic Order Quantity ordering
Ordering only when the shelf is empty
correct: Periodic review, order-up-to (R, S)
questions.explanation: A fixed review day and a variable order quantity up to a target level is the periodic review (R, S) policy.

questions.text: In simple exponential smoothing, what happens when α is increased from 0.2 to 0.8?
options: The forecast reacts faster to recent sales, but also follows random ups and downs
The forecast becomes smoother and slower to react
The forecast ignores the latest month
The forecast error always goes down
correct: The forecast reacts faster to recent sales, but also follows random ups and downs
questions.explanation: With α = 0.8, 80% of the new forecast comes from the latest month, so the forecast follows recent sales closely, including random noise.

questions.text: Over six months, the bias (average of Actual − Forecast) is +250 packs. What is the risk?
options: Forecasts are usually too low, so stock-outs are likely
Forecasts are usually too high, so extra stock will pile up
There is no risk, since a positive bias means the forecast is accurate
There is no risk as long as MAPE is below 10%
correct: Forecasts are usually too low, so stock-outs are likely
questions.explanation: A positive bias means actual sales are, on average, higher than the forecast. Stock planned on this forecast will fall short.

questions.text: A warehouse holds stock worth ₹30 lakh. Its annual cost of goods sold is ₹3.65 crore. What is its days of inventory?
options: 30 days
12 days
73 days
10 days
correct: 30 days
questions.explanation: Daily COGS = ₹3.65 crore ÷ 365 = ₹1 lakh. DOI = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days. Turnover = 365 ÷ 30 = about 12 times a year.

questions.text: Which statement about class A items in ABC analysis is correct?
options: They are a small number of items that make up most of the consumption value, so they need the closest control
They are the items with the highest number of units sold
They are low-cost items that can be bought in bulk
They are slow-moving items that should be cleared
correct: They are a small number of items that make up most of the consumption value, so they need the closest control
questions.explanation: ABC ranks items by annual consumption value, not units. A few items, such as basmati rice and sunflower oil at Madavi Warehouse, carry most of the value.
